safety.title: Flood Safety
safety.subtitle: Practical steps for individuals and families — before, during and after a flood.
safety.urgentTitle: If a flood is happening now
urgent: Move to higher ground when instructed or when water is rising near you.
Never walk, swim or drive through floodwater — even shallow, slow water.
Follow official evacuation orders immediately; take your emergency kit.
Stay away from drains, culverts, bridges, riverbanks and fast-flowing water.
Avoid fallen power lines and electrical equipment in or near water.

before.title: Before a flood
items: Monitor official weather and flood warnings (IMD, CWC, local authorities).
Learn your local evacuation routes and the nearest shelter locations.
Prepare an emergency kit (see the checklist below) and keep it ready.
Store documents and critical items in waterproof packaging.
Keep emergency contacts written down and accessible offline.
Plan for older adults, children, people with disabilities and pets.
Charge mobile phones and backup batteries/power banks.
Follow instructions from local authorities regarding evacuation.

during.title: During a flood
items: Move to higher ground when instructed or when immediate danger requires it.
Follow official evacuation orders without delay.
Never walk, swim or drive through floodwater.
Stay away from fast-flowing water, drains, culverts, bridges and riverbanks.
Avoid touching electrical equipment or fallen power lines in flooded areas.
If safe to do so, turn off electricity and gas before evacuating — never enter floodwater to reach a switch.
Keep away from damaged buildings and contaminated water.
Keep children close and help vulnerable family members.
Contact emergency services if trapped or facing an immediate threat.
Signal for help from a safe location if communication is limited.
during.warn: Climbing onto roofs or entering isolated structures is not a universal safe action — it depends on your situation and local emergency instructions.

trapped.title: If trapped indoors
items: Move away from rising water to the safest available higher level.
Do not enter dangerous, unstable or enclosed low-lying areas.
Call emergency services (112) when possible.
Share your exact location and details with rescuers.
Avoid enclosed spaces where electrical or structural hazards may exist.
Signal for help from a safe, visible location.
trapped.warn: Basements and enclosed low-lying spaces can fill with water and become deadly during flooding — do not shelter in them.

after.title: After a flood
items: Return only when authorities say the area is safe.
Avoid floodwater and contaminated surfaces.
Treat fallen power lines and damaged electrical systems as dangerous.
Do not turn on electrical systems until they have been inspected where necessary.
Use safe drinking water and follow public-health advisories.
Avoid eating food contaminated by floodwater.
Wear protective footwear and gloves during cleanup.
Watch for structural damage, gas leaks and displaced animals.
Document property damage safely for insurance or assistance claims.
Seek medical attention for injuries or possible contamination.

about.title: About ResQ Bharat
about.intro: A nationwide flood-intelligence and community-response portal for India's flood-prone rivers — from the Ganga and Indus systems in the north and the Brahmaputra in the northeast to the Godavari, Krishna, Narmada, Mahanadi and the rivers of the south. It pairs satellite flood mapping and live weather with plain-language, multilingual guidance for citizens and responders.

features.satelliteDesc: Sentinel-1 SAR flood frequency and the JRC Global Surface Water dataset identify where water has repeatedly inundated land over past monsoons.
features.terrainDesc: A DEM-based river corridor keeps mapped flood zones within reach of the channel and below a height-above-river threshold, removing false highland zones.
features.weatherDesc: Open-Meteo rainfall (antecedent 3-day + 7-day forecast) is combined with static susceptibility into a transparent weighted live-risk score.
features.damageDesc: Exposed buildings and population are combined with depth–damage scenarios and Gemini-generated briefings for decision support.

about.riversIntro: Coverage now spans flood-prone river stretches and urban catchments in every Indian state and union territory. Risk, flood zones and floodplain change are computed on demand from global Earth Engine datasets and live rainfall, so any supported location returns real results — with an honest coverage badge for how much local validation backs it.
about.riversNorthTitle: North & east — Ganga, Indus and eastern rivers
about.riversNorthDesc: The Ganga main stem and tributaries (Yamuna, Gomti, Ghaghara, Gandak, Kosi, Son, Mahananda); the Indus system (Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej); and the Mahanadi, Brahmani, Baitarani, Subarnarekha and Damodar in the east.
about.riversSouthDesc: The Brahmaputra and its tributaries (Subansiri, Manas, Kopili, Lohit, Dibang, Kameng) and the Barak; the Narmada, Tapi, Chambal and Betwa in the centre; the Godavari, Krishna, Sabarmati and Mahi in the west; and the Kaveri, Penna, Vaigai, Periyar and Pamba in the south, plus coastal and urban catchments (Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata, Hyderabad, Bengaluru).
about.maturityTitle: How mature is each area's data?
about.maturityIntro: Every location computes real, per-location rainfall, terrain susceptibility and satellite observations. A coverage badge is honest about how much local validation backs it.
about.liveDesc: the susceptibility model has been validated against a documented flood here using Sentinel-1 SAR, scoring IoU ≥ 0.50. Covers the Ganga/Bihar core, the Brahmaputra valley (Assam 2026) and ~20 basins across central, west, south and east India.
about.modelledDesc: live rainfall, terrain and satellite layers run, but the area either has no documented SAR event yet or validated below the 0.50 IoU bar (e.g. Mumbai and Kochi, where the model currently under-predicts extent).
about.partialDesc: steep Himalayan / hill corridors (Siang, Teesta, Beas, Lohit), ephemeral desert rivers (Luni) and small island UTs where precise river geometry and local flood-hazard mapping are still being integrated.
about.validationP1: North Bihar remains India's most flood-prone region — the Kosi, Gandak, Bagmati and Ghaghara descend from Nepal and routinely overtop embankments during the monsoon. Assam's Brahmaputra and Barak valleys flood almost every monsoon, displacing hundreds of thousands.
about.validationP2: Each validation event is a satellite observation window: ResQ Bharat pulls the actual flood extent from Sentinel-1 SAR for that window and scores the mapped flood zones against it — reporting precision, recall and IoU. On the Flood Intelligence page you can run any of these for the selected location.
about.peopleTitle: Built for people, not just maps
about.peopleDesc: Beyond the risk maps, ResQ Bharat includes an AI Help emergency assistant and an offline-friendly Flood Safety guide (before, during and after a flood). Gemini turns the numbers into plain-language briefings and citizen alerts in multiple Indian languages, and always points people to official emergency numbers rather than inventing local details.
about.disclaimer: AI-generated analysis — please validate before operational use. This portal is a decision-support demonstrator and not an official warning service. Always follow guidance from the CWC, IMD and state disaster authorities.
